basics.name: Chinemerem Clement Okezie
basics.label: PhD Candidate, New Jersey Institute of Technology
basics.summary: PhD candidate in Civil and Environmental Engineering with over three years of interdisciplinary research experience in subsurface energy systems. Skilled in data analysis, analytical chemistry, geomechanics, fluid-rock interaction, reservoir engineering, and petrophysics. Research projects have focused on carbon capture and storage (CCS), hydrogen storage, serpentinization, geologic hydrogen, and geothermal energy.

research experience.name: GGES Lab, New Jersey Institute of Technology
research experience.summary: My Research focuses on subsurface energy systems, including geologic hydrogen production via serpentinization and hydrogen storage in porous media. Specifically, I investigate the geochemical and geomechanical processes involved in these systems, using a combination of laboratory experiments, numerical modeling, and field data analysis to better understand their behavior and optimize their performance.

research experience.name: Gulf Coast Carbon Center, University of Texas at Austin
research experience.summary: My research focused on mitigating carbon dioxide emissions through carbon capture and storage (CCS). Specifically, I worked with large field datasets from saltwater disposal wells to calibrate the predictions made for large-scale CCS projects in the Texas Gulf Coast.
